submission.justification: Selection-S1 has the highest nominal significance (4.1 sigma at 50% efficiency in the 2025 summary) but its validation-region data/MC disagreement is 35%, far above the 10% hard limit, because the jet-substructure inputs are mismodelled. It is therefore excluded. Among the remaining strategies, Selection-S3 (neural network, kinematic variables) has 6% disagreement, within tolerance, and Selection-S2 has 3%. Scanning working points with the Monte Carlo tool gives S3 significances of 3.11 (30%), 3.17 (40%), 3.43 (50%), 3.30 (60%), 3.19 (70%) sigma, peaking at 50% efficiency. S2 peaks at 2.57 sigma (50%), below S3 at every point tested. The recommendation is Selection-S3 at 50% signal efficiency, with expected significance 3.43 sigma (statistical uncertainty only). The 6% validation disagreement should be carried as a systematic uncertainty.

requirements.requirement: Selection must be one of the three strategies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Selection-S3 is listed in candidate_specs.md as the neural network on kinematic variables.

requirements.requirement: Data/MC yield disagreement in the signal-free validation region must not exceed 10% for the variables used (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: validation_region_study.md gives 6% for Selection-S3. S1 (35%) is excluded; S2 (3%) also passes but gives lower significance.
Recommended working point is 50% signal efficiency.

requirements.requirement: Goal: highest possible expected signal significance
requirements.evidence: Among compliant options, S3 at 50% gives 3.43 sigma, the highest of the S3 and S2 scans (S2 peak 2.57 sigma). S1 would reach 4.1 sigma in the 2025 summary but violates the validation constraint. Statistical uncertainty only.
